recent_misconceptions.label: Distance-to-Sun Season Fallacy
recent_misconceptions.why: You selected distance from the Sun as the primary cause of summer/winter. This is a common intuitive bias because heat sources feel warmer when closer.
recent_misconceptions.common_intuition: Earth is physically closer to the Sun during summer and farther during winter.
recent_misconceptions.scientific_reality: Earth's 23.5° axial tilt causes sunlight to hit hemisphere angles directly (summer) vs spread out (winter). Distance variation is negligible.
recent_misconceptions.correction: Seasons are caused by Earth's axial tilt changing the angle and duration of solar insolation.
recent_misconceptions.verification_check: If orbital distance caused seasons, what would happen in Australia when it is summer in the USA?
verification_options: Australia would also be in summer (both hemispheres simultaneously warm)
Australia would be in winter (hemispheres have opposite seasons)
Australia would experience no seasonal changes
Australia's seasons would lag by 6 months
